text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia will accept diplomatic ties with Belgrade but only without conditions, says Mirza Hajric, adviser to the Moslem chairman of the collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic.

- Bosnian Croat police from the western part of the divided town of Mostar beat up an editor of the Bosnian Moslem national weekly Ljiljan, Zehrudin Isakovic, and his friend as they were driving through western Mostar.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton will probably visit Bosnia soon, diplomatic sources say. Clinton anounced the trip at a recent meeting with Izetbegovic.
- Bosnian Croat Democratic Union says Moslem-Croat federation House of Representatives should not convene until municipal government is formed in the central town of Usora.

- Although members of presidency have agreed on a common currency, the structure of a central bank and budgets for the country and entities remain unresolved, says Kasim Omicevic, governor of the National bank of Bosnia.
- Bosnian Serb side agrees that the words "Central Bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina" will be written on the new country's currency, Omicevic says.

- All inhabitants of Moslem-Croat federation are, as of Sunday, again able to directly dial international telephone numbers after a five-year pause caused by the Bosnian war, state postal company says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
